sentences.text:
The present appeal has been filed under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 ("Act of 1996" for short), arising out of the order passed by the District Court dated 03.04.2021,
whereby the District Court has allowed the application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 and set aside the award of the Arbitrator-cum-Commissioner, Rewa Division, Rewa in the matter of assessment of compensation for acquisition of land under the National Highways Act, 1956 ("Act of 1956" for short).
2. The arbitration proceedings in question are proceedings under Section 3- G(5) of the Act of 1956.

3. The basic facts leading to the present appeal are that initially there was an award of the Land Acquisition Officer dated 04.09.2013 against which the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18182 2 AA-44-2021 land loser approached the Arbitrator-cum-Commissioner of Revenue Division on 13.11.2016 and the Commissioner passed the award on 15.02.2018, thereby enhancing the compensation.

Against the said award of the Commissioner, application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 was filed by the M.P. Road Development Corporation ( "MPRDC" for short) through its Divisional Manager and the said application has now been allowed by the District Court vide order dated 03.04.2021 on two grounds.

Firstly, that the MPRDC, which is the beneficiary of acquisition, was not impleaded by the Commissioner during the proceedings and secondly that the proceedings before the Commissioner were barred by limitation.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the respondent-MPRDC has vehemently argued that the respondent-MPRDC was not heard by the Commissioner during the course of arbitration proceedings because MPRDC was not impleaded as party during the arbitration proceedings before the Commissioner and, therefore, the award has been rightly set aside by the District Court.

It is further contended that the general law of limitation as per Article 137 of the Limitation Act,
limitation would be three years from the date of accrual of cause of action and since the cause of action accrued with award of Land Acquisition Officer dated 04.09.2013, therefore, the application filed before the Commissioner on 13.11.2016 seeking arbitration was clearly barred by limitation as it was filed three years two months and ten days after accrual of cause of action.
5.

Upon considering the aforesaid assertions, so far as the question of MPRDC not being impleaded is concerned, the MPRDC approached the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18182 3 AA-44-2021 District Court under Section 34 by filing application and it is the Divisional Manager,
Sidhi of MPRDC who filed the application before the District Court.

From a perusal of the award of Commissioner, it is evident that the Divisional Manager of MPRDC had been called by the Commissioner as witness and he submitted a reply dated 16.08.2017 before the Commissioner and raised certain objections.

The Commissioner dealt with the objections of Divisional Manager of MPRDC, which is evident from para 5 and 7 of the award of Commissioner in very detail and therefore, it is clear that the MPRDC had actively participated in proceedings before the Commissioner.

The Divisional Manager of the MPRDC, who is the same person who filed application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 before the District Court, having participated in proceedings before the Commissioner in the course of arbitration proceedings, now MPRDC cannot turn back and say that it was not impleaded before the Commissioner.

6. The District Court, while deciding the application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996, was required to take a pragmatic and justice oriented view of the matter, more so when it was dealing with the case of a land loser.
The scope of Section 34 of the Act of 1996 is very limited.

Section 34 is as under:-
"34. Application for setting aside arbitral award .--(1) Recourse to a Court against an arbitral award may be made only by an application for setting aside such award in accordance with sub-section (2) and sub-section (3).

(2) An arbitral award may be set aside by the Court only if-- (a) the party making the application [establishes on the basis of the record of the arbitral tribunal that]--
(i) a party was under some incapacity, or (ii) the arbitration agreement is not valid under the law to which the parties have subjected it or, failing any indication thereon, under the law for the time being in force; or Surya Pratap Singh vs The Divisional Manager M.P on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183204327/

(iii) the party making the application was not given proper notice of the appointment of an arbitrator or of the arbitral proceedings or was otherwise unable to present his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18182 4 AA-44-2021 case; or (iv) the arbitral award deals with a dispute not contemplated by or not falling within the terms of the submission to arbitration, or it contains decisions on matters beyond the scope of the submission to arbitration:
Provided that, if the decisions on matters submitted to arbitration can be separated from those not so submitted, only that part of the arbitral award which contains decisions on matters not submitted to arbitration may be set aside; or (v) the composition of the arbitral tribunal or the arbitral procedure was not in accordance with the agreement of the parties, unless such agreement was in conflict with a provision of this Part from which the parties cannot derogate, or, failing such agreement, was not in accordance with this Part; or (b) the Court finds that-- (i) the subject-matter of the dispute is not capable of settlement by arbitration under the law for the time being in force, or (ii) the arbitral award is in conflict with the public policy of India.

Explanation 1.--For the avoidance of any doubt, it is clarified that an award is in conflict with the public policy of India, only if,--
(i) the making of the award was induced or affected by fraud or corruption or was in violation of section 75 or section 81; or (ii) it is in contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law; or (iii) it is in conflict with the most basic notions of morality or justice.

Explanation 2.--For the avoidance of doubt, the test as to whether there is a contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law shall not entail a review on the merits of the dispute.
(2A) An arbitral award arising out of arbitrations other than international commercial arbitrations,
may also be set aside by the Court, if the Court finds that the award is vitiated by patent illegality appearing on the face of the award:
Provided that an award shall not be set aside merely on the ground of an erroneous application of the law or by reappreciation of evidence.

(3) An application for setting aside may not be made after three months have elapsed from the date on which the Surya Pratap Singh vs The Divisional Manager M.P on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183204327/
3 party making that application had received the arbitral award or, if a request had been made under section 33, from the date on which that request had been disposed of by the arbitral tribunal:
Provided that if the Court is satisfied that the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application within the said period of three months it may entertain the application within a further period of thirty days, but not thereafter.

sentences.text:
(4)
On receipt of an application under sub-section (1), the Court may, where it is appropriate and it is so requested by a party, adjourn the proceedings for a period of time determined by it in order to give the arbitral tribunal an opportunity to resume the arbitral proceedings or to take such other action as in the opinion of arbitral tribunal will eliminate the grounds for setting aside the arbitral award.

(5) An application under this section shall be filed by a party only after issuing a prior notice to the other party and such application shall be accompanied by an affidavit by the applicant endorsing compliance with the said requirement.

(6) An application under this section shall be disposed of expeditiously, and in any event, within a period of one year from the date on which the notice referred to in sub-section (5) is served upon the other party."

7. The MPRDC having actively participated in the course of proceedings before the Commissioner,
its officer having entered in the witness box, it NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18182 5 AA-44-2021 having filed objection and reply before the Commissioner, now it cannot be stated by MPRDC that it was not heard because it was not impleaded before the Commissioner.
Therefore, the order of the District Court, to that extent, holding that the MPRDC did not get any opportunity, is perverse.
It deserves to be and is hereby set aside.

8. So far as the limitation part is concerned, it has been held by the Division Bench of Kerala High Court in the case of National Highways Authority of India Vs. P.V. George (WA No. 1600 of 2022) ,
that law of limitation would not apply to arbitrations under the National Highways Act, 1956.

entities.text: National Highways Authority of India Vs. P.V. George (WA No. 1600 of 2022)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Division Bench held as under :-
"6.
It is clear from Section 2(4) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act that Section 43 will not apply to every arbitration under any other enactment.
This means that if no limitation is prescribed under any other enactment, provisions of the Limitation Act would not apply to such arbitration under such enactment.

In the light of the above,
we are of the view that Limitation Act will not apply for arbitration under the National Highway Act."

9. Even otherwise, in the present case, in the application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996, it had not been set up by the respondent No.1 - MPRDC that the proceedings before the Arbitrator were barred by limitation and this ground was not taken by the respondent - MPRDC before the District Court and since this ground was not raised before the District Court, for that reason also, the District Court which was not dealing with any original proceedings but was dealing with challenge to the award, was not required to go into the matter because it was not raised by the respondent No.1 Surya Pratap Singh vs The Divisional Manager M.P on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183204327/
4

entities.text: Surya Pratap Singh vs The Divisional Manager M.P
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: when it had got an NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18182 6 AA-44-2021 opportunity to challenge the award of Commissioner before the District Court.

The District Court in its limited jurisdiction under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 could not have fished out any ground which was not taken by the party and the party had given up that ground by not taking the said ground in its memorandum of application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996.
The entire application of MPRDC before the District Court was hardly of one page or so and no such ground was taken by the MPRDC before the District Court.
10. Therefore, the District Court could not have held the arbitration proceedings before the Commissioner as barred by limitation.
To that extent also, the order deserves to be and is hereby set aside.
11. Consequently, the impugned order passed under Section 34 by the District Court deserves to be and is hereby set aside.
The award passed by the Commissioner is brought back to life.
The land loser shall be at liberty to get the said award enforced.
12. Appeal is allowed.
